state_program_name: OPWDD-certified Individualized Residential Alternative (IRA), supervised or supportive community residence, with residential habilitation paid under the OPWDD HCBS waiver (Medicaid)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its OPWDD-certified Individualized Residential Alternative (IRA) at **[SITE ADDRESS]**, and any supervised or supportive community residence it operates under an OPWDD operating certificate. Residential habilitation in these homes is paid under the OPWDD Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waiver (Medicaid).

The manual does the following:

- **Meets the written-policy requirement.** 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(2) requires each community residence to develop and implement written policies and procedures on the listed topics "at a minimum." This manual is [AGENCY NAME]'s response to that requirement and is the document OPWDD reviews at survey and certification.
- **Protects the people we support.** The policies cover rights, health and safety, protective oversight, medication, personal funds, behavior support, and the prevention, reporting and investigation of abuse, neglect and incidents. They are written to protect each person's dignity, choice, privacy and safety.
- **Gives staff clear direction.** Direct support professionals, supervisors, managers and the governing body can see what is required, who is responsible and what to do.
- **Supports compliant waiver billing.** Documentation and rate-code requirements for IRA residential habilitation are set out so that claims can withstand OMIG audit.
- **Is open to the people it affects.** Under 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(3) the manual is available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others.

This manual is a template. It becomes [AGENCY NAME]'s policy only after it has been customized, adopted and put into practice, as described in "How to Use This Manual."
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize it before use
This manual is written for a New York OPWDD-certified IRA (supervised or supportive). It contains placeholders such as **[AGENCY NAME]**, **[SITE ADDRESS]**, and role titles. Before adoption you must:

- Replace every placeholder with the agency's actual name, site details, titles, phone numbers and procedures.
- Fit each policy to the actual home: supervised or supportive IRA type, certified capacity, the number of people served, any temporary use beds, and whether the site is in New York City.
- Delete provisions that do not apply. For example, supportive-residence additions apply only to supportive residences, and the 635-7.3 requirements apply only to IRAs of nine or more persons.
- Complete the site-specific written protective oversight plan and evacuation plan that 14 NYCRR 686.16 requires. These are individual to the site and cannot be copied from this manual.

### 2. Adopt it formally
The agency's governing body (board of directors, or the managers or members of an LLC) must review and formally adopt the manual. Record the adoption date, the vote and the version number on the approval page. Keep the minutes.

### 3. Keep it current
- Assign a named owner, **[POLICY OWNER TITLE]**, to review the manual at least annually and whenever a regulation, OPWDD guidance, the operating certificate, the site, or agency practice changes.
- Record every revision in a revision log and have the governing body adopt material changes.
- Check sources marked in this manual as unverified, pending or dated against the current official text before relying on them. These include OPWDD ADM #2014-01, OPWDD ADM #2002-01, the OPWDD memo on representative payees (new 14 NYCRR 633.9 and conforming changes to 633.15), the Jonathan's Law notice timeframes, the OPWDD ADM #2012-02 numeric drill minimums, and NYC DOB TPPN #9/94. Section 14 NYCRR 633.27 (Training Flexibilities) is expired and must not be used as a basis for any policy.
- Do not rely on a printed or saved copy that has been superseded. The current adopted version must be the one available at the site.

### 4. Train staff on it
- Every employee, intern, volunteer, consultant and contractor whose work touches the home must be trained on the parts of the manual that apply to their role. Do this at hire, when policies change and at least annually.
- Training required by regulation, such as 14 NYCRR 633.8 and 633.17, must be completed in full. Keep training records that show type, frequency and amount, with current records available at interview (633.8(b)(3)).
- Staff sign an acknowledgment that they have received, read and been trained on the manual. Keep the acknowledgments in personnel files.

### 5. Make it available
Keep a current copy at the residence and make it available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others, as 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(3) requires.

### 6. Structure and the Appendix A crosswalk
- The manual is organized by topic and follows the numbering of the regulations where possible, so a reviewer can trace each policy to its citation.
- **Appendix A is the crosswalk.** It lists every item on the official documents the state uses to review this manual (see "Regulatory Framework") and names the policy section that satisfies each. When you add, move or delete a policy, update Appendix A.
- Each policy section states its purpose, who it applies to, the procedure, who is responsible, the documentation to keep, and the regulatory citation.

### 7. Use with other required documents
This manual does not replace the individual's person-centered plan, the site-specific protective oversight plan, the staffing schedule, the volunteer utilization plan (if volunteers are used), or the facility evacuation plan. It refers to them and requires that they be kept.

### 8. Questions and conflicts
If this manual conflicts with a regulation or a current OPWDD directive, the regulation or directive controls. Contact the OPWDD regional office or Division of Quality Improvement listed in the Regulatory Framework when a requirement is unclear.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

This manual is built on the rules and guidance below. Each is cited by its exact cite text. Where a source is marked as dated, unverified or pending, confirm its current status before relying on it.

### A. Certification, classes and the IRA
- **14 NYCRR 619.2**: classes of operating certificates (supervised community residence, supportive community residence, IRA).
- **14 NYCRR 686.99**: Part 686 glossary (IRA, supervised IRA, supportive IRA, protective oversight).
- **14 NYCRR 686.16**: certification of the IRA class. It covers building and life-safety standards by capacity, the site-specific written protective oversight plan, the facility evacuation plan, supervisor first-aid training, and site selection under MHL 41.34.
- **14 NYCRR 686.15**: temporary use beds and vacant beds (applies to IRAs through 686.16(a)(4)).
- **14 NYCRR 686.9**: staffing, including the staffing plan, the written staffing schedule, and the volunteer rules.
- **Mental Hygiene Law 41.34**: site selection, as applied to IRAs by 14 NYCRR 686.16(a)(7).
- **OMR 248; 14 NYCRR Parts 620, 624, 633, 635, 636, 671, 686**: IRA operating certificate application and the Parts it draws on.

### B. Physical plant, fire and life safety
- **14 NYCRR 635-7.1, 635-7.2, 635-7.4**: physical plant, Life Safety Code and environmental requirements referenced by 686.16, and Uniform Code enforcement for IRAs via 635-7.4(a)(3).
- **14 NYCRR 635-7.3**: safety and welfare requirements (IRAs housing nine or more persons), including quarterly testing of heat and smoke-detecting alarm devices.
- **OPWDD ADM #2012-02**: minimum frequency of evacuation and fire drills. The numeric minimums must be taken from the ADM text.
- **NYC DOB TPPN #9/94**: IRA Certificate of Occupancy in New York City. The current status is unverified, so confirm with DOB.

### C. Rights, person-centered planning and admission
- **14 NYCRR 633.4**: rights and responsibilities of persons receiving services.
- **14 NYCRR Subpart 636-1 (incl. 636-1.4)**: person-centered planning and documentation of rights modifications.
- **OPWDD Health and Safety Alert (July 2018) - HCBS Settings 'access to food'; 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi); 14 NYCRR 636-1.4**: access to food in HCBS settings.
- **14 NYCRR Subpart 636-3; 24-ADM-03**: admission to and services in certified residential opportunities.
- **14 NYCRR 636-3.5**: responsibilities of care management providers.
- **OPWDD Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity**: DDRO Director approval before any admission.

### D. Staffing, training, background checks
- **14 NYCRR 633.8**: training of employees, volunteers, family care providers and persons receiving services on safety and the prevention of abuse.
- **14 NYCRR 633.27**: [Expired] Training Flexibilities. **Not to be relied on.** Staff must complete the full 633.8 and 633.17 training.
- **14 NYCRR 633.22**: criminal history record checks.
- **NYS Justice Center Criminal Background Check (CBC) program; MHL 16.33**: designation of Authorized Persons and fingerprinting.
- **Mental Hygiene Law 16.34**: criminal history checks for prospective OPWDD employees and volunteers. The statute text was not reviewed in preparing this manual.

### E. Health, medication and behavior support
- **14 NYCRR 633.17**: medication (including vitamins).
- **14 NYCRR 633.16**: protection of individuals receiving services (behavior support and restrictive or intrusive interventions). The operative subdivisions must be reviewed in the official text.

### F. Incident management and abuse prevention
- **14 NYCRR 624.4**: notable occurrences, defined.
- **14 NYCRR 624.5**: reporting, recording, and investigation.
- **OPWDD Part 624 and Part 625 Handbook (updated 2/16/23)**: OPWDD guidance on reportable incidents.
- **NYS Justice Center - Mandated Reporters (VPCR hotline)**: mandated reporter duties. The 24-hour VPCR hotline is **1-855-373-2122** (Relay: dial 711 and give the number).
- **NYS Justice Center - What to Expect if You Are Involved in a Justice Center Investigation (Oct 2021)**: reporting timing and Category 2 findings.
- **Jonathan's Law (per NYS Justice Center Investigations Guidance, 2025)**: notification and access to incident information. The statute section and notice timeframes must be confirmed in the statute and 624.5.

### G. Personal funds and cost of care
- **14 NYCRR 633.15**: management of personal funds.
- **14 NYCRR 635.9; SSL 131-o**: personal allowance and room and board cost responsibilities.
- **OPWDD Personal Allowance Manual (2023) and Protecting Personal Allowance advisory (Oct 2023)**: personal allowance guidance.
- **OPWDD memo to provider associations (Sept 2026) - new 14 NYCRR 633.9 / conforming changes to 633.15**: representative payee rulemaking. This is pending. Confirm the adopted text before finalizing the funds policy.

### H. Waiver services, billing and enrollment
- **14 NYCRR Subpart 635-10 and Part 671; 10 NYCRR 86-10.2**: residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD HCBS waiver.
- **10 NYCRR 86-10.3**: rates for residential habilitation services.
- **OPWDD ADM #2014-01**: supervised IRA residential habilitation (daily unit, rate codes, retainer days). Its continuing effect is not confirmed.
- **OPWDD ADM #2002-01**: IRA residential habilitation service documentation. It is dated, and the supportive IRA minimum is status-unverified.
- **OMIG Audit Protocol - OPWDD IRA Residential Habilitation**: documentation and rate-code audit standards.
- **eMedNY OPWDD Waiver Provider Enrollment; Community Residence enrollment (category of service 0269)**: provider enrollment.

Phone numbers and emails are listed only where the source material supplied them. For the others, use the website shown or ask the OPWDD regional office.

### Official policy checklist and review documents

OPWDD has no single policy checklist form for this manual. The state's review items are taken from the regulation sections that list required written policies and plans:

1. **14 NYCRR § 686.6 - Administration** (policy/procedure manual content required of each community residence). This is the primary source. Section 686.6(a)(2) requires policies and procedures on the listed topics "at a minimum," and 686.6(b)(3) lists the manual contents OPWDD surveys for. Under 686.6(a)(3) the manual is available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others. 14 NYCRR 686.6 is not named in the 686.16(a)(4) list of Part 686 sections that an IRA must meet. It is applied here because 686.6(a)(2) covers "each community residence" and 14 NYCRR 619.2 treats IRAs as a community residence type. Confirm this with the OPWDD regional office.
2. **14 NYCRR § 686.16 - Certification of the facility class known as individualized residential alternative.** This section requires the site-specific written protective oversight plan and the facility evacuation plan that OPWDD verifies.
3. **14 NYCRR § 686.8 - Program for supportive community residences.** This applies **only to supportive** residences. It adds referral, intake, admission and discharge-criteria policies and other items for the manual required by 686.6(a)(2).

The **IRA Operating Certificate Application (OMR 248)** is also part of OPWDD's review. It could not be retrieved while this manual was prepared. Obtain the current form from OPWDD and check it against Appendix A. Also verify the 686.6, 686.8 and 686.16 text against the official NYCRR (Department of State) text, because the copies used may not be the latest. Confirm the current submission method and review procedure with the OPWDD regional office or Division of Quality Improvement, since these are prescribed by OPWDD through the certification process under 14 NYCRR Part 619 (see 686.2(d)).

**Appendix A maps every official item** on these documents to the specific policy in this manual that satisfies it, using the regulation's own numbering, so that OPWDD reviewers and agency staff can find each requirement quickly. Items that OPWDD verifies as plans or survey checks, not manual topics (for example, the individual protective oversight plans and the fire-evacuation evaluation in each person's ISP), are identified in Appendix A with the document or record where they are kept.

### Adoption, maintenance and training

- **Customize.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other placeholders and fit each policy to the actual home.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the adoption.
- **Keep current.** Review at least annually and on any change in law, guidance, certification or operations. Do not rely on expired provisions such as 14 NYCRR 633.27.
- **Train.** Staff must be trained on the manual and on the required regulatory training (14 NYCRR 633.8, 633.17 and the others listed above), with training records kept.

citations.title: Classes of operating certificates
citations.requirement: Lists the OPWDD operating certificate classes for community residences: supervised community residence, supportive community residence, and individualized residential alternative (IRA).

citations.title: Part 686 Glossary (IRA, supervised IRA, supportive IRA, protective oversight)
citations.requirement: Defines IRA and the supervised and supportive IRA types. A supervised IRA has staff onsite or proximately available whenever residents are present.

citations.title: Certification of the facility class known as individualized residential alternative
citations.requirement: (a)(2)-(3): 9+ persons must meet 635-7.1, 7.2 and 7.3. 8 or fewer persons must meet the 635-7.1(h)(1)(ii) building code (NYC: 635-7.1(i)(1)(ii)) and 635-7.4(b)(3). If occupants cannot evacuate in 3 minutes or less, 635-7.2(a)(1)(iii) also applies. (a)(4): an IRA must meet 686.1-686.5, 686.9, 686.15(a)(1)-(3) and 686.16. (a)(5)-(6): protective oversight appropriate to need, with a site-specific written plan covering assessment of each person's supervision need (staff and/or technology), trained substitutes, supervisor qualifications and training, and periodic review. (a)(7): MHL 41.34 site selection applies to 4-14 bed IRAs with onsite supervision and 1-3 bed IRAs with 24-hour supervision. (b): OPWDD verifies the facility evacuation plan, staff and resident training and evaluation, a current fire-evacuation evaluation in each ISP (8 or fewer beds), an annual review of each person's protective oversight plan, supervisor first-aid training, and fire alarms audible in sleeping areas with doors closed (8 or fewer beds).

citations.title: Utilization of temporary use beds and vacant beds
citations.requirement: IRAs of four or more beds may designate temporary use beds on the operating certificate. Temporary use beds count toward certified capacity. 686.15(a)(1)-(3) applies to IRAs through 686.16(a)(4).

citations.title: Staffing (community residences)
citations.requirement: (a)(1)-(2): personnel must be available to supervise, operate and maintain the premises, and there must be a staffing plan based on the number of individuals, their level of functioning and need, support staff needs and physical plant demands. (a)(3): volunteers may not substitute for paid personnel. Family and friends are not counted as volunteers. (a)(4): in a supervised residence, staff must be available whenever individuals are present. Less intensive coverage is allowed only on a documented individual assessment in the plan of services. (b)(1): a written staffing schedule at the site shows supervision available or on call 24 hours a day. (b)(2): a written volunteer utilization plan if volunteers are used. The rule sets no numeric ratio.

citations.title: Physical plant, Life Safety Code and environmental requirements referenced by 686.16; Uniform Code enforcement for IRAs via 635-7.4(a)(3)
citations.requirement: Building, Life Safety Code and environmental standards that 686.16 incorporates for IRAs. NYS DOS guidance identifies 635-7.4(a)(3) as the Uniform Code enforcement route for OPWDD IRAs.

citations.title: Safety and welfare requirements for all facilities (except family care homes and IRAs housing eight or fewer persons)
citations.requirement: Applies to supervised community residences and IRAs housing nine or more persons. One listed requirement is documentation that all heat and smoke-detecting alarm devices are tested quarterly (635-7.3(e)(i)(1)).

citations.title: Rights and responsibilities of persons receiving services
citations.requirement: (a)(3): rights limitations must be documented, individual, time-limited and for clinical purposes only. (a)(4): enumerated rights (safe and sanitary environment; freedom from abuse, corporal punishment, unnecessary mechanical restraint and unnecessary medication; confidentiality; written individualized plan with right to participate, object and appeal; choice of physician and dentist; sexuality and family planning information; religion; voting; use of personal money; balanced diet; own clothing; privacy; storage; request an alternative residence; grievances without reprisal; visitors and communication; health care proxy; gender expression). (a)(4)(xv): information before admission on supplies and services provided and charges. (a)(6): staff are advised of rights. (a)(7): rights are not limited for staff convenience, as a threat, as retribution or for discipline. (a)(8): rights and conduct rules are given at or before admission and after changes, in the primary language. (a)(9): objections under 633.12. (a)(10): written requests for clinical record access under MHL 33.16, with denial review by the OPWDD Clinical Record Access Review Committee. (a)(11): health care proxy duties. (a)(12): advise of complaint contacts on admission and as they change. (a)(15): language access with no charge for interpreters.

citations.title: Training of employees, volunteers, family care providers and persons receiving services with regard to their safety and the prevention of abuse
citations.requirement: (b)(1): training within 3 months of hire or start of volunteering on human growth and development, characteristics of persons served, promoting positive relationships, abuse prevention/identification/reporting/processing, laws and policies on protection from abuse, incident reporting, and safety and security procedures including fire safety. (b)(2): annual retraining on positive relationships, abuse prevention and reporting, laws and policies, incident reporting, and safety/security including fire safety. (a)(1)(viii)-(ix): training on preventing and managing significant-risk body substance exposure (HIV). (b)(3): a mechanism to monitor type, frequency and amount of training, with current records and employee concurrence on interview. (a)(2), (b)(4): self-protection training for individuals identified by the program planning team. (b)(5): one-time board training applies only to not-for-profit corporations.

citations.title: Management of personal funds
citations.requirement: Applies to all OPWDD-certified residential facilities. Policies must reflect the agency's fiduciary duty under MHL 33.07(e) when it manages funds. Policies must address at minimum security, staff accountability, paper and electronic recordkeeping, usage, and monitoring of personal allowance and other income. Personal allowance is the monthly income portion for the individual's personal expenditure. Management is the SSL 131-o offer to set up separate accounting. Records of compliance are kept 4 years per OPWDD's regulations page. Only excerpts of the section were retrieved.

citations.title: Protection of individuals receiving services in facilities operated and/or certified by OPWDD (behavior support)
citations.requirement: Applies to all OPWDD-certified residential facilities. Definitions reviewed: behavior plan/human rights committee; informed consent committee; functional behavior assessment; behavior support plan as a component of the plan of services; restrictive/intrusive interventions (intermediate and restrictive physical intervention, exclusionary time-out, mechanical restraining devices, behavior medication without a co-occurring psychiatric diagnosis, and other agency-designated methods); physical intervention categories (protective, intermediate, restrictive); modified clothing as a mechanical restraint; rights limitations; aversive conditioning; Level 1 and Level 2 Behavioral Intervention Specialist qualifications; program planning team composition. Operative subdivisions (d)-(j) were not retrieved.

citations.title: Medication (including vitamins)
citations.requirement: Required of all residential facilities. Each agency develops its own medication policies. Staff may administer only if they hold a job description with direct care duties and have completed an OPWDD-approved course and practicum and been certified or recertified within the year (a)(14)(iii)(c). Medical or nursing supervision of medication staff is required (a)(15). A program planning team evaluates self-administration ability with RN, physician or PA input, no later than 3 months after admission, and reviews it at least annually (a)(16). A separate administration record per person (name, medication/dose/route, date/time, signature) is required (a)(17). Annual medication regimen review by an RN, physician, PA or pharmacist (a)(18). Locked storage; double-locked controlled substances (non-supportive residences); separate locked container for medications in a food refrigerator (a)(19). OTC medication needs written practitioner approval at least annually and is limited to 2 days without practitioner direction (a)(13). Medication is suspended and the practitioner told immediately on a significant adverse reaction (a)(14)(ii). Disposal rules in (a)(20) were only partly retrieved.

citations.title: Criminal history record checks
citations.requirement: Applies to OPWDD-certified facilities and HCBS waiver services. (c)(1): designate authorized parties and submit their name, position and contact information to the Justice Center. (c)(2): written policies covering which applicants are subject to checks, safety and oversight of temporarily approved provisional staff and volunteers, notification to the Justice Center when a party ceases to be a subject party, and handling of later convictions or pending charges. (d)(2): checks are required for prospective employees and operators (natural persons with an ownership interest) with regular and substantial unsupervised contact. This is presumed for direct care in residential facilities (ICFs, CRs, IRAs), residential habilitation staff, supervisors of direct care staff, drivers and escorts, clinicians, care managers, and anyone assigned to a certified site. Also required on a change in ownership. (e): process under Part 701 (701.5). (f): provisional approval is allowed only without unsupervised physical contact, with monitoring by a trained employee and an attestation. Only the first part of the section was retrieved.

citations.title: [Expired] Training Flexibilities
citations.requirement: The Cornell LII Part 633 table of contents lists this section as [Expired]. The earlier research described commissioner flexibilities during extreme staffing shortages. Do not build any policy on it. Staff must complete the full 633.8 and 633.17 training.

citations.title: Notable occurrences, defined
citations.requirement: On and after 1/1/2016: serious notable occurrences are (a) the death of any person receiving services regardless of cause, including all deaths of residents of OPWDD-certified residences, and (b) sensitive situations, which agency policy must define and which include possible criminal acts by an individual. Minor notable occurrences are suspected theft or financial exploitation over $15 and up to $100 (isolated, no card involved) and injury needing treatment beyond first aid by a physician, dentist, PA or NP. A death that is also a reportable incident is reported both ways. The pre-2016 text, retained in the section, covered unauthorized absence, choking and larger thefts, which are now reportable incidents under 624.3.

citations.title: Reporting, recording, and investigation
citations.requirement: (a)(1): written policies on reporting, recording, investigation, review and monitoring; the reporting duties of employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors; and notice to employees that every reportable incident is investigated and that an investigation continues to a substantiated or unsubstantiated finding even if the employee leaves. All employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors must report. Minor notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee within 48 hours. Reportable incidents and serious notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee immediately, and to OPWDD immediately. IRMA updates are due at least monthly until closure. Only the first part of the section was retrieved from search text.

citations.title: The Part 624 and Part 625 Handbook
citations.requirement: OPWDD guidance. Reportable incidents in OPWDD-certified programs go to the Justice Center VPCR at 1-855-373-2122 and to OPWDD under 624.5. Deliberate inappropriate use of restraints is abuse/neglect. Inappropriate use of restraints is a significant incident.

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center - Mandated Reporters (VPCR hotline)
citations.title: Mandated Reporters
citations.requirement: Employees and volunteers of certified or operated facilities are mandated reporters. They report when they have reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident, via the 24-hour VPCR hotline at 1-855-373-2122 (Relay: dial 711 and give the number).

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center Criminal Background Check (CBC) program; MHL 16.33
citations.title: Criminal Background Check (CBC)
citations.requirement: Providers designate Authorized Persons to register applicants for fingerprinting (IdentoGO) and receive results.

citations.title: Criminal history checks for prospective OPWDD employees and volunteers
citations.requirement: OPWDD providers request checks for prospective employees and volunteers, submitted through OPWDD per the Justice Center CBC page. The statute text was not fetched; the cite and its application are taken from the research and the Justice Center page.

citations.title: Person-centered planning; Documentation of rights modifications
citations.requirement: From OPWDD's final regulation text, effective 11/1/2015. Applies to OPWDD-funded HCBS waiver services. The plan must document, for a certified residential setting, that the residence was chosen by the individual and which alternatives were considered. The plan is updated when it is ineffective and on reassessment of functional need. 636-1.4: modifications to the specified HCBS rights need a specific assessed need and justification in the person-centered service plan. 633.4 and 633.16 hold the related documentation rules.

citations.title: Admission to and services in certified residential opportunities
citations.requirement: Subpart 636-3 (effective 3/14/2023) governs admission. OPWDD assigns Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need. Certified residences must promptly report vacancies so each is first considered for people with Emergency Need.

citations.title: Responsibilities of care management providers
citations.requirement: Care managers confirm OPWDD eligibility and a residential request before referral.

citations.title: Residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: Defines residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD 1915(c) HCBS waiver. Providers must be approved by OPWDD and DOH and be Medicaid-enrolled to be paid.

citations.title: Rates for residential habilitation services
citations.requirement: One provider-wide residential habilitation rate per provider.

citations.title: Supervised IRA residential habilitation: daily unit, rate codes, retainer days
citations.requirement: Daily unit of service. Rate codes cover service day, therapeutic/non-medical leave day and retainer/medical leave day. At most 14 retainer days per person per rate year. Research flags that it is not confirmed still in effect.

citations.title: IRA Residential Habilitation Service Documentation
citations.requirement: Dated guidance on IRA residential habilitation documentation. Research flags the supportive IRA 11-day minimum as status-unverified. Confirm it is current before use.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol - OPWDD IRA Residential Habilitation
citations.title: OMIG audit protocol
citations.requirement: OMIG audits IRA residential habilitation claims for documentation and rate-code compliance. A claim is disallowed if the documentation does not match the rate code billed.

citations.title: Personal allowance and room and board cost responsibilities
citations.requirement: Sets resident room and board and cost-of-care responsibilities and the personal allowance. For community residences including IRAs, the maximum monthly cost of care is the Level II SSI combined payment level minus the SSL 131-o minimum personal allowance. Supervised IRAs are responsible for required supplies and services under 635.9.

citations.cite: OPWDD Personal Allowance Manual (2023) and Protecting Personal Allowance advisory (Oct 2023)
citations.title: Personal allowance guidance
citations.requirement: Providers must have written procedures to handle, store and audit personal allowance. Staff are trained on them. Each person's funds are tracked separately. Funds are locked with limited access and staff accountability. There is a ledger of all receipts, disbursements and cash balance. Cash equivalents such as prepaid cards are treated as cash. Cash above the cash cap needs documentation of a specific purpose and is limited to 14 days. Annual personal expenditure planning is required when the agency manages the allowance.

citations.title: Fire safety: evacuation and fire drill frequency
citations.requirement: Standardizes minimum frequencies of evacuation and fire drills in homes and day settings. Evacuation and fire drills are generally procedurally synonymous. Drills may be varied for a few specific reasons, but the minimum number of full evacuation drills must still be met. Homes certified under the Health Care chapters of the Life Safety Code cannot use defend-in-place for non-fire evacuations. The numeric minimums were not captured, so pull the ADM text.

citations.cite: OPWDD Health and Safety Alert (July 2018) - HCBS Settings 'access to food'; 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi); 14 NYCRR 636-1.4
citations.title: Access to food in HCBS settings
citations.requirement: Individuals are entitled to access to food at any time. Restrictions run from least restrictive (all foods, all the time) to most restrictive through the person-centered planning process, and must be justified under 636-1.4.

citations.title: IRA Operating Certificate Application
citations.requirement: IRA operating certificate application. Listed processing time is 90 to 120 days. The term is triennial, with a maximum of 3 years. Denials are based on the inspection outcome.

citations.cite: eMedNY OPWDD Waiver Provider Enrollment; Community Residence enrollment (category of service 0269)
citations.title: Provider enrollment
citations.requirement: Enrollment requires an IRS SS-4 letter (a W-9 is not accepted) and certification of a Provider Compliance Program. Community residence enrollment is filed under category of service 0269.

citations.title: IRA Facilities
citations.requirement: A 1994 NYC DOB notice tied the final Certificate of Occupancy for IRAs to the IRA license. Current status is unverified, so ask DOB.

citations.title: Site selection (as applied to IRAs by 14 NYCRR 686.16(a)(7))
citations.requirement: Applies to IRAs of 4-14 beds with onsite supervision and 1-3 beds with 24-hour supervision, per 686.16(a)(7). The statute text was not fetched.

citations.cite: OPWDD memo to provider associations (Sept 2026) - new 14 NYCRR 633.9 / conforming changes to 633.15
citations.title: Representative payee rulemaking
citations.requirement: OPWDD is amending Part 633 to add or amend 633.9 on representative payees for residents of certified residences, with conforming changes to 633.15 on managing personal allowance. Confirm the adopted text before finalizing the funds policy.

citations.cite: Jonathan's Law (per NYS Justice Center Investigations Guidance, 2025)
citations.title: Notification and access to incident information
citations.requirement: Jonathan's Law requires notification and access to information about incidents at OPWDD-certified, operated or licensed providers. The statute section number is not stated in the retrieved text. Pull the statute and 624.5 for notice timeframes.

citations.cite: OPWDD Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity
citations.title: DDRO Director approval of placements
citations.requirement: Every placement into a certified residence requires approval of the DDRO Director before admission, using OPWDD's request form.

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center - What to Expect if You Are Involved in a Justice Center Investigation (Oct 2021)
citations.title: Mandated reporter timing; Category 2 findings
citations.requirement: A mandated reporter with reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident reports immediately to the VPCR. Reporting may be delayed for safety or to call 911, but the report must be made within 24 hours of discovery. A final Category 2 finding is reported to OPWDD providers in the Staff Exclusion List check. It is not an automatic bar to employment but is a factor in the hiring decision.

policies.title: Referral, Need Determination and Admission Decision
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Residence Manager, admission review team members, nursing staff and all staff who receive referrals or take part in admission decisions at [AGENCY NAME]'s OPWDD-certified Individualized Residential Alternative (supervised or supportive).
policies.purpose: To make sure every admission to [AGENCY NAME]'s IRA follows OPWDD's admission rules. Each applicant has a documented need for service, a decision that the agency can meet that person's ongoing needs, the participation of staff and the applicant, and the required DDRO Director approval before admission.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(2), which requires each community residence to develop and implement written policies and procedures, and 686.6(a)(2)(i), Admission.

(1) Need determination (686.6(a)(2)(i)(a)). [AGENCY NAME] determines each applicant's need for service, whether the agency can meet the person's ongoing needs, and how much weight to give family intactness and the geographic proximity of the family. The Admission Review Team records its findings on each of these three questions in writing. Family proximity is one factor the team considers. It is never a reason to exclude someone on its own, and it never overrides the applicant's own choice.

(2) Participation (686.6(a)(2)(i)(b)). Residence staff and the applicant must take part in the determination, including the final decision on admission. The applicant is invited to meet the team and visit the residence. The applicant is supported, with accommodations and with a parent, guardian, correspondent or advocate of the applicant's choosing, to give views and ask questions. No admission decision is final until the applicant's views are recorded.

(3) Procedures for obtaining admission (686.6(a)(2)(i)(c)). Admission follows the numbered procedures below. Under 14 NYCRR Subpart 636-3 and 24-ADM-03, OPWDD assigns a priority level of Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need. [AGENCY NAME] promptly reports each vacancy so that it is first considered for people with Emergency Need.

(4) Required documents and approvals. The care manager must confirm OPWDD eligibility and a residential request before referral (14 NYCRR 636-3.5). Staff ask for this documentation with every referral and do not process a referral without it. Every placement requires the approval of the DDRO Director, using OPWDD's Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity, before the person is admitted. Staff never move a person in on a promise of later approval.

(5) Rights. Admission and the person's rights are handled consistently with 14 NYCRR 633.4. Voluntary admission, nondiscrimination and charge disclosure are in ADM-03. Admission criteria and pre-admission records review are in ADM-02.

definitions.term: Emergency Need, Substantial Need, Current Need
definitions.definition: The priority levels OPWDD assigns to people seeking certified residential opportunities under 14 NYCRR Subpart 636-3 and 24-ADM-03.

The group that evaluates a referral: the Administrator or designee, the Residence Manager, the nurse or health care coordinator, a direct support professional who knows the residence, the applicant, and, with the applicant's agreement, the parent, guardian, correspondent and care manager.
The Director of the OPWDD Developmental Disabilities Regional Office, who must approve every placement into a certified residence before admission.
The person or organization responsible for care management for the individual. The care manager confirms eligibility and the residential request before referral.
A person designated to receive notices and communications for the individual, such as a family member, friend or advocate.

procedures: Referral intake: The Administrator or designee ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [PHONE]) logs every referral on the Referral Log on the day it is received. The log records the date, source, applicant name, care manager and contact details.

Eligibility documentation: On the day of receipt, staff confirm the referral packet includes the care manager's documentation of OPWDD eligibility and of the applicant's request for residential services (14 NYCRR 636-3.5). If either is missing, staff write to the care manager the next business day to request it. The referral is marked 'incomplete' and goes no further until the documents arrive.
Priority level: Staff record the OPWDD-assigned priority (Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need) in the referral file. If it is not stated, staff ask the care manager to supply it.

Vacancy reporting: Whenever a vacancy exists or is expected, the Administrator reports it to OPWDD promptly. The agency standard is by the next business day after the vacancy is known, so that the vacancy is first considered for people with Emergency Need. The date and the recipient of the report are logged.

Referral screening: Within [NUMBER] business days of a complete referral, the Administrator reviews it against the written admission criteria in ADM-02. If it is clearly outside the criteria, the Administrator sends the referral source a written explanation citing the specific criterion.

Pre-admission contact: Staff contact the applicant and the parent, guardian or correspondent, as available. They explain the program, arrange a visit to the residence, and offer to visit the applicant where the applicant now lives.

Communication support: Before any meeting, staff ask about the applicant's communication needs and primary language. They arrange interpreters or communication supports at no charge to the applicant and note them in the file (see RIT-03).

Admission Review Team meeting: The Administrator convenes the team with the applicant. The team completes the Need Determination Worksheet, which records (a) the applicant's need for service, (b) whether the residence can meet the person's ongoing needs, including health, behavioral, supervision and accessibility needs and staffing, and (c) family intactness and geographic proximity of the family and how they bear on the person's needs and choices.

Compatibility and resources: The team considers the needs of the current residents and the residence's resources (staffing, physical plant, nursing and clinical supports). It does not use these considerations to exclude anyone on a basis prohibited in ADM-03.

Applicant participation: The applicant or the person's supporter gives views at the meeting. The Residence Manager records whether the applicant wants to move in, and the applicant signs or otherwise indicates agreement on the Participation Record. If the applicant does not agree, the process stops and ADM-03 (no admission over objection except by court order) applies.

Records review: Before the final decision, the team completes the pre-admission records review in ADM-02. The review is documented in the admission file before any request for DDRO approval is submitted.

Team decision: The team states its recommendation in writing (accept, accept with conditions, or decline), with its reasons and each member's signature or concurrence. Staff and the applicant take part in the final admission decision. The Administrator signs the final decision.

DDRO request: If the decision is to accept, the Administrator submits OPWDD's Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity to the DDRO Director. The submission includes the supporting documentation OPWDD requires. The request date is logged. The person is not admitted until written approval is received and filed.

Notice of decision: Within [NUMBER] business days of the decision, the Administrator gives the applicant, parent, guardian or correspondent and care manager written notice of the decision. If the answer is no, the notice gives the reasons in plain language and explains how to ask for review (see APP-01).

Admission day: After DDRO approval, the Residence Manager gives the rights and conduct rules, complaint contacts and written charge notice in ADM-03. The person's choice of this residence and the alternatives considered are recorded in the person-centered plan (REC-01).

Quality review: The Administrator reviews the Referral Log quarterly. The review covers the time from referral to decision, the number of referrals declined and the reasons, and vacancy reports, and the findings go to the quality improvement process (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the admission process. Logs referrals, reports vacancies to OPWDD, convenes the team, signs the final decision and submits the DDRO request.
Takes part in the review, supports the applicant's visit and participation, and gives the admission-day rights and charge information.
Advises the team on whether the residence can meet the applicant's health needs and reviews health information (ADM-02, HS-02).
Takes part in the process, including the final admission decision, with the supports the applicant chooses.
Confirms OPWDD eligibility and the residential request before referral and supplies the priority level and assessments.
Approves each placement before admission.

documentation: Referral Log, with the dates of receipt, vacancy reports and decisions
Care manager documentation of OPWDD eligibility and residential request
OPWDD priority level (Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need) in the referral file
Need Determination Worksheet and Admission Review Team minutes
Participation Record signed or otherwise indicated by the applicant
Copy of the Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity and the DDRO Director's written approval
Written notice of decision to the applicant, guardian or correspondent and care manager
Vacancy reports sent to OPWDD
All of the above are kept in the individual's admission file (REC-08).

policies.title: Admission Criteria and Pre-Admission Review
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Residence Manager, nursing staff and the Admission Review Team at [AGENCY NAME]'s OPWDD-certified IRA.
policies.purpose: To state the applicant criteria in functional terms and to require review of a current medical/physical examination and current assessments before any person is found eligible for admission. This ensures that admission decisions rest on recent information.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(2)(i)(d) (applicant criteria, in functional terms, for admission) and 686.6(a)(2)(i)(e)(1)-(2) (review of the results of a medical/physical examination and of assessment(s) of strengths, needs, interests and living skills, each conducted within 90 days prior to the review).

(1) Criteria in functional terms (686.6(a)(2)(i)(d)). [AGENCY NAME] describes who it can serve by what the person can do and what support the person needs. The criteria do not rest on a diagnosis label. The written criteria are in the Admission Criteria Statement, which the Administrator keeps current and which is part of this manual. Criteria are stated in the following form:
- The applicant is an adult aged [AGE RANGE] who has been determined by OPWDD to be eligible for services.
- The applicant needs [supervised: 24-hour staff presence and individualized protective oversight / supportive: periodic staff support and an assessed need for less than continuous supervision], as shown by the supervision-need assessment (IRA-02, SUP-01).
- The applicant needs help with some or all of the following: [medication management, meal preparation, personal care, money management, community travel, health care appointments].
- The residence can provide the applicant's assessed level of supervision, personal care and health support with its available staff and nursing oversight.
- The applicant can be supported to evacuate or get to safety with the evacuation supports the residence provides (EMR-02, IRA-04).
- The residence's physical plant can meet the person's mobility and accessibility needs (HS-07).
The Admission Criteria Statement may limit the age range, level of disability or gender only when necessitated by the overall objective of the facility, as ADM-03 permits. Any such limit is written down and explained in the statement.

(2) Pre-admission review (686.6(a)(2)(i)(e)). To decide that an applicant meets the criteria, the team must review both of the following before admission: (1) the results of a medical/physical examination conducted within 90 days before the review, and (2) one or more assessments of the applicant's strengths, needs, interests and living skills completed within 90 days before the review. If either document is older than 90 days on the date of the review, the team does not conduct the review until a current one is obtained.

(3) Timing and approval. The review is documented in the admission file before the Administrator requests DDRO Director approval (ADM-01). The DDRO request is not submitted until the documented review is on file. This policy is part of the admission procedures under 14 NYCRR Subpart 636-3.

definitions.definition: Criteria expressed as the supports a person needs and the abilities the person has (for example, help with medications or ability to travel independently), rather than by diagnosis alone.
The date on which the Admission Review Team meets to decide whether the applicant meets the admission criteria. The 90-day periods are counted back from this date.
An examination by a licensed health care practitioner within 90 days before the review date, with results the nurse can review.

definitions.term: Assessment of strengths, needs, interests and living skills
definitions.definition: A written assessment, by the care manager, prior provider or agency staff, of what the person does well, needs help with, and likes, including daily living skills.

procedures: Criteria maintenance: Each January, and whenever the program changes, the Administrator reviews the Admission Criteria Statement. The review checks that every criterion is expressed in functional terms and that the criteria are applied equally to all applicants. Changes follow POL-02.

Packet request: When a complete referral is received (ADM-01), the Administrator or designee asks the care manager, or the applicant and guardian, for the most recent medical/physical examination results and the most recent assessment(s) of strengths, needs, interests and living skills. The request goes out within [NUMBER] business days.

Date check: Before scheduling the review, the Residence Manager writes the review date on the Pre-Admission Review Checklist. For each document, the Residence Manager records the document's date and calculates the number of days between that date and the review date.

Currency rule: If either the examination or the assessment is more than 90 days old on the review date, the Residence Manager marks it 'not current'. The review is postponed, and the Residence Manager requests an updated examination or assessment with the applicant's consent.
Reschedule rule: If the review is rescheduled, the Residence Manager repeats the date check against the new review date.

Nursing review of examination: The nurse or health care coordinator reads the examination results and writes a brief summary. The summary covers diagnoses, medications, allergies, treatments, dietary needs, seizure or choking risks, mobility needs and any needs for nursing oversight. The summary is given to the team.

Assessment review: The Residence Manager and a direct support professional read the assessment(s) with the applicant, where the applicant wishes, and summarize strengths, needs, interests and living skills, including supervision needs.

Criteria comparison: The team compares the applicant's functional profile to each admission criterion on the checklist and records 'met' or 'not met', with a short explanation. If the applicant has not been assessed for supervision need, the team follows IRA-02 or SUP-01 as applicable.

Meeting the needs: For each identified need, the team writes down how the residence will meet it (staffing, nursing, training, equipment, community supports). If it cannot, the team records the reason and does not recommend admission unless the gap can be closed before the move-in date.
Sign-off: The Administrator, nurse and Residence Manager sign and date the checklist. The signed checklist, the examination, the assessment(s) and the nursing summary are filed in the admission file.
DDRO gate: Staff do not send the Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity to the DDRO Director (ADM-01) until the Administrator has confirmed that the signed checklist is in the file.

Hold between approval and move-in: If the move-in date is delayed after DDRO approval, the Residence Manager rechecks with the Administrator whether significant changes in the person's health or needs have occurred. If so, the team repeats the review before admission.

Annual audit: Each year the Administrator audits a sample of admission files, and every admission in the year if there were fewer than five. The audit confirms that each file contains a review completed within the 90-day period and documented before the DDRO request. The audit results go to the quality improvement process (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the Admission Criteria Statement, ensures the review is completed and documented before any DDRO request, and audits files annually.
Requests records, checks the 90-day dates, completes the checklist and keeps the admission file.
Reviews the medical/physical examination and states whether the residence can meet the health needs.
Compares the applicant's functional profile to the criteria and records the results.

documentation: Admission Criteria Statement, written in functional terms, with the date of last review
Pre-Admission Review Checklist with the date of the examination, the date of the assessment(s) and the review date
Medical/physical examination results dated within 90 days before the review
Assessment(s) of strengths, needs, interests and living skills dated within 90 days before the review
Nursing summary of the examination
Signed team sign-off, filed before the DDRO request (see ADM-01)
Annual admission-file audit report

policies.title: Voluntary Admission, Nondiscrimination and Written Disclosure of Charges
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Residence Manager, business office staff and all staff who take part in admission or who talk with applicants, individuals and families about admission, rights or charges at [AGENCY NAME]'s OPWDD-certified IRA.
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
policies.purpose: To ensure that admission is voluntary, that no one is excluded on a prohibited basis, and that every applicant and the applicant's family or guardian receive, before admission and as changes occur, a written statement of charges and the supplies and services the residence provides.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(2)(i)(f), (g) and (h).

(1) Voluntary admission (686.6(a)(2)(i)(f)). No person is admitted to [AGENCY NAME]'s residence over his or her objection, except by a court order. If an applicant objects or appears unwilling, staff stop the admission process. They do not proceed on the word of a family member, provider or agency alone. A person who has a guardian is still asked for his or her own views, and any objection is recorded and passed to the guardian and the care manager. Staff admit a person over objection only on presentation of a court order, which is filed.

(2) Nondiscrimination (686.6(a)(2)(i)(g)). No person is excluded from the residence on the basis of race, religion, color, age, gender, national origin, or inability to pay for services. [AGENCY NAME] follows the Americans with Disabilities Act and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act, and provides reasonable accommodations and language access (RIT-03). The written Admission Criteria Statement (ADM-02) may limit the age range, level of disability or gender of the people served only when this is necessitated by the facility's overall objective. Any such limit is written down with the reason before it is used.

(3) Written disclosure of charges and services (686.6(a)(2)(i)(h)). Before admission, and again as changes occur, each applicant, or the parent, guardian or correspondent as available, receives written notice of (a) any charges (see 14 NYCRR 686.12), and (b) the supplies and services the facility provides (see 14 NYCRR 686.13). The notice is also required by 633.4(a)(4)(xv). If the applicant is a capable adult who objects to the notice being given to others, the notice goes to the applicant only and the objection is recorded.

(4) Content of the charge notice. The charges described must be consistent with 14 NYCRR 635.9 and SSL 131-o. For community residences, including IRAs, the maximum monthly cost of care is the Level II SSI combined payment level minus the SSL 131-o minimum personal allowance. [AGENCY NAME] does not charge more than the maximum, does not reduce the personal allowance, and, as a supervised IRA, provides the supplies and services that 635.9 requires it to be responsible for. The notice must state the supplies and services included in the charge, so that the person is not billed separately for items the agency must provide.

(5) Rights and conduct rules. The rights of the individual and the conduct rules of the residence are given at or before admission, and again after any change, in the person's primary language (633.4(a)(8)). Interpreters are provided at no charge (633.4(a)(15)). On admission the person is also told how to reach the persons and agencies to whom complaints may be made, and is told again when those contacts change (633.4(a)(12)).

definitions.definition: A written order of a court with jurisdiction directing a person's placement, which is the only basis for admission over the person's objection.
A person identified by the individual to receive notices and information on the individual's behalf, as available.
The resident's share of room, board and related costs, limited by 14 NYCRR 635.9 and SSL 131-o as described in this policy.
An adult who has no guardian or other legal substitute decision-maker for the matter at issue and who can understand and decide, with supports as needed.
The language the person uses and understands best, including sign language and other communication methods.

procedures: Voluntariness check: At the first meeting and again on the admission day, the Residence Manager asks the applicant privately, using accessible language, whether he or she wants to live in the residence. The answer is written on the Voluntary Admission Form and signed or otherwise acknowledged by the applicant.

Objection response: If the applicant says no, or shows reluctance that cannot be resolved, the Residence Manager stops the process and tells the Administrator the same day. The Administrator notifies the care manager and guardian in writing, and does not schedule admission.

Court order: If a placement is claimed to rest on a court order, the Administrator obtains a copy, confirms it with the care manager or the court, and files it before any admission over objection. Staff do not take part in a placement over objection that lacks the order.

Nondiscrimination screening: At the close of each referral, the Administrator records the reason for any decision to decline. The Administrator reviews the reason against the prohibited bases (race, religion, color, age, gender, national origin, inability to pay) and signs that none was a factor.

Limits on criteria: Before the Admission Criteria Statement includes any limit on age range, level of disability or gender, the Administrator documents why the limit is necessitated by the residence's overall objective. The governing body approves it under POL-02.

Language and communication: Before admission, the Residence Manager finds out the person's primary language and communication method. The Residence Manager arranges interpreters, translated documents, large print or other formats at no charge to the person (RIT-03).

Charge notice preparation: Before the admission meeting, the Administrator and business office prepare the Notice of Charges and Services. It lists (a) each charge, with amount, due date and how it is calculated; (b) the supplies and services the residence provides as part of its program, including those 14 NYCRR 635.9 requires of a supervised IRA; (c) the personal allowance and who controls it (REC-02); and (d) any items for which the person may choose to pay extra.

Charge check: The Administrator compares the monthly cost of care in the notice to the current maximum under 635.9 and SSL 131-o (the Level II SSI combined payment level minus the SSL 131-o minimum personal allowance), and signs the calculation sheet. The business office does not issue a notice that exceeds the maximum.

Delivery before admission: At least [NUMBER] days before admission whenever possible, and in any event before the person moves in, the notice is given in writing, and explained verbally, to the applicant and to the parent, guardian or correspondent as available. The person who gives it records the date, the persons who received it and the language used.

Capable adult objection: If a capable adult asks that the notice not be given to others, the Residence Manager records the request on the form, gives the notice to the individual only, and notes that the guardian or correspondent was not notified at the person's request.

Rights and conduct rules: At or before admission, the Residence Manager gives the person the written rights (14 NYCRR 633.4) and the conduct rules of the residence, in the person's primary language, and goes through them in a way the person can understand. The person or supporter signs receipt. Staff tell the person that signing is not a condition of admission.

Complaint contacts: At admission, the Residence Manager gives the person the contact information for the persons and agencies to which complaints may be made, including the agency's grievance contact [GRIEVANCE CONTACT NAME AND PHONE] and OPWDD, (866) 946-9733, 44 Holland Avenue, Albany, NY 12229-0001 (APP-02). Updated contacts are given again whenever they change.

Changes in charges or services: Whenever charges, or the supplies and services provided, change, the Administrator issues a written notice of the change in the same way, before the change takes effect where possible, and files the notice.

Questions and review: The Residence Manager offers to meet the person and family to answer questions. A person who disagrees with a charge may use the grievance procedure (APP-02) or the review process (APP-01). No retaliation follows.

Audit: Each year the Administrator audits admission files for a signed Voluntary Admission Form, charge notice, rights receipt and complaint contact acknowledgment. The results go to the quality improvement process (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures admissions are voluntary and nondiscriminatory, approves the charge calculation and notices, and audits files.
Confirms the person's willingness, delivers the rights, conduct rules, complaint contacts and charge notice, and arranges language access.
Prepares charge notices consistent with 14 NYCRR 635.9 and SSL 131-o and never bills above the maximum.
Approves any admission criteria that limit age, disability level or gender (POL-01, POL-02).

documentation: Signed Voluntary Admission Form and any court order
Declination log with nondiscrimination review sign-off
Notice of Charges and Services, with the cost-of-care calculation sheet, delivery date, recipients and language used
Record of any capable adult's objection to notice to others
Signed receipt of rights and conduct rules, with the date given and the language used
Record that complaint contacts were given, and any later updates
Annual admission-file audit

policies.title: Discharge Criteria and Avoiding Precipitous Discharge
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Residence Manager, nursing and clinical staff, program planning team members and direct support staff at [AGENCY NAME]'s OPWDD-certified IRA.
policies.purpose: To state the criteria under which a person may leave the residence, and to ensure that [AGENCY NAME] makes and documents reasonable efforts to meet a person's needs before a more restrictive placement is sought or discharge is contemplated.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(2)(ii), Discharge, including 686.6(a)(2)(ii)(a) (criteria for discharge of individuals) and 686.6(a)(2)(ii)(b) (reasonable efforts to avoid precipitous discharge).

(1) Discharge criteria (686.6(a)(2)(ii)(a)). A person is discharged from the residence only when one of the following applies:
- The person (or the person's guardian, where one acts for the person) chooses to move, including a request for an alternative residence under 14 NYCRR 633.4(a)(4).
- The person's assessed needs have changed so that the residence cannot meet them, even with reasonable efforts and additional supports, and the program planning team, with the person, agrees that a different setting or level of service is needed.
- The person's need for a more or less restrictive or intensive setting is shown by the person's assessments and plan of services, and an alternative that is appropriate has been identified.
- A court orders it.
- The person dies (EMR-03).
In all other cases, discharge is not used. In particular, discharge is not used as a form of discipline, as retaliation for a complaint or grievance, or for the convenience of staff (633.4(a)(7)).

(2) Avoiding precipitous discharge (686.6(a)(2)(ii)(b)). Before a more restrictive placement is sought and before discharge is contemplated, [AGENCY NAME] must make reasonable efforts to meet the person's needs. In deciding what is reasonable, the team considers the needs of the other individuals in the residence and the residence's available resources. Efforts, and the reasons that any effort was not feasible, are documented.

(3) Person-centered planning. Plans and discharge decisions follow 14 NYCRR Subpart 636-1. The plan is updated when it is ineffective and on reassessment of functional need, and it records the choice of residence and the alternatives considered. A person has a right to participate in, object to and appeal any decision (APP-01).

(4) Vacancy report. A discharge that creates a vacancy is reported to OPWDD promptly under 14 NYCRR Subpart 636-3 and 24-ADM-03, so the vacancy is first considered for people with Emergency Need (ADM-01).

definitions.definition: A discharge or request for a more restrictive placement made without first making and documenting reasonable efforts to meet the person's needs in the residence.

The person, the person's guardian or correspondent as available, the care manager, residence staff, nursing and clinical staff, and others the person chooses, who develop and review the person's plan of services.
A setting that offers more supervision, structure or limits on freedom than the person has in the residence.
Documented supports and changes tried, or considered and found unworkable, that are proportionate to the person's needs and the residence's available resources.

procedures: Early warning: Any staff member who believes a person's needs may no longer be met in the residence tells the Residence Manager the same day. The Residence Manager records the concern in the Concern Log and informs the Administrator within one business day.

Team meeting: Within [NUMBER] business days, the Residence Manager convenes the program planning team, including the person and the person's chosen supporters. The team identifies the specific need or problem, using current data (incident reports, behavior data, health records, assessments).

Clinical and nursing input: The nurse or health care coordinator reviews health issues (HS-02, HS-03). If behavior is involved, the behavior support clinician reviews the data and the positive behavior support plan (BEH-01). The team documents their findings.

Options considered: The team lists the supports and changes it will try or has considered. Examples: staffing adjustments or added supervision; training for staff on the person's needs; changes to the plan of services or to the person's routine; adaptive equipment or environmental changes; additional nursing, therapy, behavioral or day service supports requested through the care manager; a room change; added community or family supports.

Resources and other residents: The team records what resources are available in the residence and the effect on other residents. The team does not rely on general statements. It writes the particular fact for each consideration.

Action plan: The team writes an action plan with named persons, due dates and measures of success, and sets a review date no later than [NUMBER] days later. The person and supporters receive a copy in a form they can understand.

Implementation and tracking: The Residence Manager makes sure the action plan is carried out and records progress in the daily documentation and in the Concern Log. Changes to the plan of services follow REC-01.
Review: At the review date the team determines whether the efforts worked. If so, the concern is closed. If not, the team may extend or alter the efforts, and documents why.

Stopping point: Only after the team has documented reasonable efforts may the Administrator discuss with the person, the guardian or correspondent and the care manager whether a different placement is needed. The discussion is recorded.

Person's own request: If the person asks to move, or asks for an alternative residence at any time, staff do not delay. The Residence Manager tells the Administrator and the care manager the same business day and starts the procedures in DIS-02.

No improper use: The Administrator reviews every proposed discharge to confirm that it is not discipline, retaliation for a grievance or complaint, or for staff convenience. The Administrator signs the review.
Moving to DIS-02: When the team concludes that discharge is necessary and one of the criteria above is met, the team documents the decision and starts the discharge procedures in DIS-02.
Vacancy report: On learning of a vacancy through discharge, the Administrator reports it to OPWDD promptly, by the next business day as the agency standard, and logs the report (ADM-01).
Tracking: The Administrator reports quarterly to the quality improvement process (GOV-02) on the number of discharges and requests for discharge, the reasons, the efforts made, and the outcomes.

responsibilities.duty: Applies the criteria, confirms reasonable efforts were documented before any step toward a more restrictive placement, and reports vacancies.
Convenes the team, carries out the action plan and keeps the records.
Assesses health-related needs and recommends supports.
Reviews behavior data and revises behavior supports (BEH-01).
Identifies and tries reasonable alternatives and makes the recommendation with the person.
Take part in every decision, may request an alternative residence at any time, and may object and appeal.

documentation: Written discharge criteria (this policy)
Concern Log entries and team meeting minutes
Assessments, nursing and clinical review notes
Action plan with dates, responsible persons and results
Evidence of reasonable efforts and of any considered effort found unworkable, with reasons
Administrator's review that discharge is not for discipline, retaliation or staff convenience
Updated person-centered plan (REC-01)
OPWDD vacancy report and log
Quarterly discharge summary to quality improvement

policies.title: Discharge Procedures, Freedom to Leave and Discharge Planning
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Residence Manager, program planning team members, nursing staff and all direct support staff at [AGENCY NAME]'s OPWDD-certified IRA.
policies.purpose: To set out how a person is discharged, including when the discharge is against the recommendation of the program planning team, to protect a person's freedom to leave, and to ensure that those responsible for program planning help design and coordinate the discharge plan.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 14 NYCRR 686.6(a)(2)(ii)(c), (d) and (e).

(1) Procedures for being discharged (686.6(a)(2)(ii)(c)). Discharge follows the numbered procedures below. A discharge may take place only when a criterion in DIS-01 is met. The person and the person's parent, guardian or correspondent, as available, receive advance written notice in the person's primary language (633.4(a)(8)), with information on the right to object (633.4(a)(9)).

Discharge against the recommendations of the program planning team. If the person (or the person's guardian) wishes to leave against the team's recommendation, or if the agency proposes a discharge the person opposes or the team does not support, the Administrator personally reviews the case. [AGENCY NAME] records the team's recommendation and the reasons. It tells the person the possible risks and alternatives, and tells the person about the right to object and appeal. It does not obstruct a person who has the right to decide to leave. A discharge that the person opposes goes ahead only after the review and objection process in APP-01 (14 NYCRR 633.12) is complete, unless there is an immediate danger to health or safety requiring emergency action under EMR-01 or a court orders otherwise. The agency documents the discussion, the decision and who made it.

(2) Freedom to leave (686.6(a)(2)(ii)(d)). No overt or covert physical or psychological pressure is applied to prevent a person who wants to leave from doing so. Staff do not threaten, bargain, withhold belongings, funds or medication, delay paperwork, use guilt, or make statements about consequences in order to stop a person from leaving. Staff may offer information, safety planning, and the choice to meet with the team. If a person leaves in a way that puts the person at immediate risk, staff follow BEH-03 and EMR-01. This does not permit coercion.

(3) Discharge planning (686.6(a)(2)(ii)(e)). Those responsible for program planning, including the person, the care manager, residence and nursing staff and clinical staff, take part in designing the discharge plan and coordinating services for a person who is being discharged. The plan follows the person-centered planning requirements of 14 NYCRR Subpart 636-1, and records the setting chosen and the alternatives considered.

(4) Rights during discharge. The person's rights under 14 NYCRR 633.4 apply until the day of discharge, including confidentiality, use of personal money, the right to own clothing and belongings, the right to make a grievance without reprisal, and a request for an alternative residence.

definitions.definition: A written plan, prepared with the person and the program planning team, for the person's move to a new setting. It covers services, health care, medications, funds, belongings and follow-up.

definitions.term: Against the recommendation of the program planning team
definitions.definition: A discharge, or a decision to leave, that the team does not recommend.
Open or hidden physical or psychological means (such as threats, intimidation, withholding of belongings or funds, deception or delay) used to stop a person from leaving.
A formal expression by the person, guardian or correspondent of disagreement with a discharge or placement decision, handled under 14 NYCRR 633.12 (see APP-01).

procedures: Starting the discharge: A discharge begins only after the Administrator confirms in writing that a criterion in DIS-01 is met, or that the person has asked to leave. The Residence Manager opens a Discharge File the same day.

Notice to person and supporters: The Residence Manager or Administrator gives the person, and the parent, guardian or correspondent as available, written notice in the person's primary language. The notice explains the reason, the proposed date and destination, the person's right to object and appeal under APP-01, and the grievance and complaint contacts (APP-02). It is also explained in person, with interpreters or communication supports at no charge. Notice to others is not given if a capable adult objects.

Care manager and OPWDD: The Administrator notifies the care manager the same business day and works with the care manager on the discharge destination and services. The Administrator reports the resulting vacancy to OPWDD promptly (DIS-01, ADM-01).

Planning meeting: Within [NUMBER] business days of the notice, the Residence Manager convenes the program planning team to design the discharge plan. The person decides who attends. Team members who are responsible for the person's program must take part, and their attendance is recorded.

Discharge plan content: The plan lists the destination and the person's choice of it, the services and supports to be in place, health care providers and appointments, medications and treatments, dietary needs, behavior supports, transportation, who will meet the person, funds and belongings, and a follow-up contact. It states which staff member is responsible for each step and by what date.

Team recommendation recorded: The team records whether it recommends the discharge. If the team does not, or if the person wants to leave against the team's advice, the Administrator carries out steps 7 and 8.

Against-recommendation review: The Administrator meets the person and supporters, explains the team's concerns and the possible risks and alternatives in plain language, and gives the person written information. The Administrator records the person's decision, the persons present and any objection raised.

Objections: If the person, guardian or correspondent objects to a discharge or placement decision, the Residence Manager accepts the objection in any form (spoken or written), writes it down and sends it to the Administrator the same day. The objection is handled under APP-01 and 14 NYCRR 633.12. The discharge does not proceed over the person's objection until that process is complete, except in an emergency under EMR-01 or by court order.

Freedom to leave: If a person says he or she wants to leave, staff listen, tell the Residence Manager or on-call administrator, and offer information. Staff do not use pressure, threats, removal or withholding of belongings, funds or medications, or misleading statements to stop the person (see RIT-01). If the person is in immediate danger, staff follow BEH-03 and EMR-01.

Health and medications: Before the move, the nurse prepares a health summary and a current medication list. The nurse arranges for the person's medications and treatment orders to go with the person as permitted by law and plan (REC-07).

Funds and belongings: The Residence Manager reconciles the person's personal funds with the person, and returns funds and an accounting at discharge (REC-02). The person's clothing, belongings and documents are inventoried against the admission inventory, packed with the person's participation and handed over with a signed receipt.

Records: With the person's consent or as the law permits, the Residence Manager sends the records the receiving provider needs, and records what was sent (REC-03, REC-08). Records are retained as required by REC-08.

Transition support: Staff accompany the person where the plan calls for it, and give the receiving provider a verbal hand-off. The Residence Manager contacts the person or the new provider within [NUMBER] days after the move and records the result.
Close-out: The Administrator reviews the Discharge File for completeness within [NUMBER] days of the discharge and signs it. The summary goes to the quality improvement process (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Confirms the criterion, handles discharges against the team's recommendation, ensures objections are processed before a contested discharge, and reports the vacancy.
Opens the Discharge File, gives notice, convenes the planning meeting and coordinates the transition.
